source.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization
source.authors: Kai-Yue Wen; Xing-Yu Dang; Kaifeng Lyu; Teng-Yu Ma; Percy Liang

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps training-token budgets and fits held-out validation loss against tokens, testing the token-scaling part of the claim in a different optimizer setting.
record.gate_note: The 130M-token-budget sweep and its fitted curves bear on V1. Other optimizer comparisons, including token-equivalent speedups and learning-rate transfer sweeps, do not report a test of the scaling-law shape; the AdamW scaling law is also used as a reference for the speedup metric rather than independently assessed there.
record.test_reason: This is an optimizer paper. It fits a token-scaling curve L = L∞ + A·N^-α on a 130M model to compare MuonW and MuonH asymptotes (Sec. 3.4, Fig. 7). It also fits an AdamW scaling law across Chinchilla ratios as the reference for its token-equivalent speedup metric. In both cases the power-law form is a measuring tool. The study reports no exponents, fit quality or residuals, and draws no conclusion on whether loss follows a power law, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Hyperball's explicit norm constraint improves the scaling behaviour of matrix-based optimizers (20–30% token-equivalent speedup at 1.2B) and makes learning-rate transfer across width and depth more reliable. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws themselves.
record.recipe_differences: Measures validation loss across training-token budgets and fits an asymptotic power-law form, but focuses on comparing optimizer variants in an overtrained setting rather than establishing general scaling laws or extrapolation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported token-scaling curves and fitted asymptotes differ between MuonW and MuonH.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted token-scaling asymptotes differ by optimizer: MuonH 3.065 vs MuonW 3.079 at 130M. The speedup of Muon over AdamW is reported as shrinking with scale under weight decay but sustained under Hyperball.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimizer and its norm-control scheme shift the fitted irreducible loss and the relative efficiency across scale.

record.problems: The token-scaling evidence is limited to one 130M-parameter model and two optimizer variants. The fit exponents and goodness of fit are not stated, and the individual validation-loss values are presented only in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted as scaling-law findings. The 1.2B optimizer comparisons and learning-rate transfer sweeps are discussed in gate_note because they do not assess the fitted loss-versus-token scaling relation.

untested.parts: Whether held-out loss follows a power law in tokens, parameters or compute. The study assumes the form; it does not assess it.
Extrapolation of small-run fits to larger runs.
Shape at fixed parameter count. The depth and width sweeps vary parameter count and target learning-rate drift.
Fit-dependence. Optimizer-dependent asymptotes are reported, but not as a test of how published laws disagree.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T1' is downgraded to 'uses_without_test/T4'. The scaling-law fits are tools for comparing optimizers, and no fit quality or exponents are reported. The AdamW reference law over Chinchilla ratios 1–8× at 1.2B is likewise used, not assessed.

versions.untested_parts: Only token scaling is examined, in one 130M-parameter model and an overtrained setting. Parameter-count and compute scaling, several-orders-of-magnitude model-size scaling, and whether the fitted form predicts larger runs are not tested.
